title: Accounting Standard 20 Earnings Per Share
outcomes: Compute earnings attributable to equity shareholders.
Compute the weighted average number of shares including bonus and rights issues.
Compute diluted EPS and identify anti-dilutive instruments.

meta.exam_tip: Write numerator and denominator separately, adjust bonus from the start, apply the rights factor only before the issue date.

concepts.title: Scope and the earnings figure for basic EPS
body: AS 20 prescribes how to compute and present EPS so that performance can be compared across periods and enterprises. It is mandatory for enterprises with equity shares listed or in the process of listing, and for others that disclose EPS.
Basic EPS = profit (or loss) belonging to equity holders for the year ÷ the time-weighted count of equity shares in issue.

Earnings are profit after tax for the period less preference dividends for the period and related tax. Cumulative preference dividend for the period is deducted whether or not declared; non-cumulative only if provided for or declared. Arrears of earlier years are not deducted again.
concepts.analogy: EPS tells each ordinary share how much of the year's profit belongs to it.
concepts.work: Unpaid cumulative preference dividend of the current year still reduces equity earnings.

concepts.title: Weighted average number of shares
body: Shares are counted from the date consideration is receivable — generally the date of issue: for cash, when cash is receivable; on conversion of debt, from when interest stops; in exchange for assets, from recognition of the acquisition.
Time-weighting factor = days (or months) the shares are outstanding ÷ days in the period.
Partly paid shares count as a fraction of a share to the extent they rank for dividend relative to a fully paid share. Contingently issuable shares are included from the date all conditions are met.
concepts.analogy: A share issued halfway through the year earns half a share's weight.
concepts.work: Shares issued on 1 January in an April–March year carry a weight of 3/12.

concepts.title: Bonus issues, splits and rights issues
body: Bonus issues, share splits and consolidations change the number of shares without changing resources. They are treated as if they occurred at the start of the earliest period presented, and earlier EPS figures are restated.
A rights issue below fair value has a bonus element. Shares before the issue are multiplied by: fair value per share immediately before exercise ÷ theoretical ex-rights fair value per share.
Theoretical ex-rights fair value = (total fair value of existing shares + rights proceeds) ÷ shares after the issue.
If such changes occur after the year end but before the Board approves the statements, EPS is still computed on the new number and this is disclosed.
concepts.analogy: Bonus shares are free slices of the same cake, so they are counted from the very beginning.
concepts.work: A 1:1 bonus halves both this year's and last year's EPS as reported.

concepts.title: Diluted EPS and anti-dilution
body: Diluted EPS assumes conversion of all dilutive potential equity shares (convertible debentures and preference shares, options, warrants).

Earnings are increased by the after-tax effect of dividends and interest on dilutive potential shares, and any other consequential changes. Shares are increased by the number that would be issued on conversion, from the start of the period or the date of issue if later.
Options and warrants: only the shares deemed issued for no consideration count — shares under option minus the number that the exercise proceeds would buy at fair value.

Potential shares are dilutive only if conversion reduces EPS from continuing ordinary operations. Anti-dilutive ones are ignored; they are tested one by one, starting with the instrument that cuts EPS the most.
concepts.analogy: Diluted EPS shows the worst-case sharing of profit if every convertible were converted.
concepts.work: Options for 10,000 shares at ₹60 when fair value is ₹80 add 2,500 shares for diluted EPS.

concepts.title: Presentation and disclosure
body: Basic and diluted EPS appear in the statement of profit and loss itself (not just the notes) for each class of equity shares with different rights, with equal prominence, for all periods presented — even if negative (loss per share).
Disclose the numerators and their reconciliation to profit, the weighted average shares used for basic and diluted EPS and their reconciliation, and the nominal value of shares.
If EPS is also given using other earnings figures, the same share numbers are used and basic and diluted figures shown with equal prominence, in the notes.
concepts.analogy: Both figures, side by side, on the face of the profit and loss statement.
concepts.work: A loss of ₹2 per share is still reported as basic and diluted EPS.

illustrations.title: Fresh issue and bonus in one year
illustrations.q: Kanchan Ltd. earned profit after tax of ₹55,00,000 in 2026-27. It has 10% cumulative preference shares of ₹10,00,000. Equity shares outstanding on 1 April 2026: 8,00,000. On 1 October 2026 it issued 2,00,000 shares for cash at full market price; on 1 January 2027 it made a 1:5 bonus issue. Compute basic EPS.

solution.text: Cumulative preference dividend is deducted whether or not declared. Bonus shares are treated as outstanding from the beginning of the period, without time-weighting.

jobs.title: EPS working for the annual report
jobs.situation: A listed client issued shares, made a bonus issue and granted employee options during the year.
steps: Compute equity earnings after preference dividend.
Time-weight new shares; adjust bonus from the start.
Test options and convertibles for dilution.
jobs.takeaway: Get the share count right before worrying about dilution.

mcqs.q: Profit after tax ₹30 lakh; 12% non-cumulative preference shares ₹20 lakh, no dividend declared. Earnings for basic EPS:
mcqs.explain: Non-cumulative preference dividend is deducted only if it is provided for or declared for the period. With no dividend declared, all ₹30 lakh belongs to equity holders. In practice: cumulative dividend would have been deducted.
mcqs.topic: Scope and the earnings figure for basic EPS

mcqs.q: Arrears of cumulative preference dividend for earlier years paid this year are:
options: Not deducted again in computing current year earnings
mcqs.explain: Only the cumulative preference dividend for the current period is deducted; arrears relating to earlier years were already deducted then. Deducting again would double count. In practice: look at the period the dividend relates to.
mcqs.topic: Scope and the earnings figure for basic EPS

mcqs.q: 6,00,000 shares at the start; 1,20,000 issued for cash on 1 January (year April–March). Weighted average shares:
mcqs.explain: The new shares are outstanding for 3 of 12 months: 6,00,000 + 1,20,000 × 3/12 = 6,30,000. Shares are counted from the date consideration is receivable. In practice: use days if dates are uneven.

mcqs.q: A 1:2 bonus issue in the middle of the year is treated as if issued:
options: At the beginning of the earliest period reported
At the end of the year
Six months before the year end
mcqs.explain: Bonus issues change only the number of shares, not resources, so they are adjusted from the start of the earliest period presented and prior EPS is restated. No time-weighting is applied. In practice: restate comparatives.
mcqs.topic: Bonus issues, splits and rights issues

mcqs.q: Fair value before rights ₹120; theoretical ex-rights fair value ₹110. The adjustment factor for shares before the rights issue is:
mcqs.explain: The factor is fair value just before exercise divided by theoretical ex-rights fair value: 120 ÷ 110 = 1.0909. It is applied to shares before the issue for the period before it. In practice: restate prior EPS by dividing by it.
mcqs.topic: Bonus issues, splits and rights issues

mcqs.q: Options over 20,000 shares at ₹50 each; average fair value ₹80. Shares deemed issued for no consideration:
mcqs.explain: Proceeds of ₹10,00,000 would buy 12,500 shares at ₹80, so the remaining 7,500 shares are treated as issued free and added for diluted EPS. In practice: only in-the-money options dilute.

mcqs.q: Interest on convertible debentures for diluted EPS is:
options: Added back to earnings net of tax
mcqs.explain: On assumed conversion, interest would no longer be paid, so earnings are increased by the after-tax interest and the shares on conversion are added. In practice: compute the incremental EPS of each instrument.

mcqs.q: A potential equity share that increases EPS on conversion is:
mcqs.explain: Potential shares are included only when they reduce EPS from continuing ordinary operations; if conversion would raise EPS, they are anti-dilutive and excluded. In practice: rank from most to least dilutive.

mcqs.q: Basic and diluted EPS are presented:
options: On the face of the profit and loss statement with equal prominence
mcqs.explain: AS 20 requires both figures in the profit and loss statement itself for each class of equity shares, with equal prominence for all periods, even when negative. In practice: show a loss per share too.

mcqs.q: Shares issued on conversion of a debenture are included in the weighted average from:
options: The date interest ceases to accrue
The date of the board meeting
mcqs.explain: For conversion of debt, shares are counted from the date interest stops accruing, as that is when the consideration is effectively received. In practice: check the conversion date in the terms.

summary: Basic EPS = equity earnings ÷ weighted average shares.
Deduct current cumulative preference dividend even if undeclared.
Time-weight issues; bonus, split, consolidation from the start.
Rights factor = fair value before ÷ TERP.
Diluted: add back after-tax interest/dividend; add conversion shares; options via treasury method.
Ignore anti-dilutive items; show both EPS with equal prominence.
remember: Restate prior EPS for bonus and rights.
traps: Arrears of earlier years are not deducted again.

viva.model: Profit or loss belonging to equity holders, divided by the weighted average count of equity shares in issue over the year.

viva.q: Why are bonus shares not time-weighted?
viva.model: Because a bonus issue splits the same resources over more shares, so it is treated as if it had occurred at the start of the earliest period presented.

viva.q: What is the bonus element in a rights issue?
viva.model: When rights are offered below fair value, part of the issue is effectively free; it is adjusted by the ratio of fair value before exercise to theoretical ex-rights fair value.
A potential share whose conversion would increase EPS, or reduce loss per share, from continuing operations; it is ignored in diluted EPS.

viva.q: How are options treated in diluted EPS?
viva.model: The shares under option are split into those that the proceeds would buy at fair value and the rest, which are treated as issued for no consideration and added to the share count.

cases.title: Vasant Ltd.
cases.case: Vasant Ltd. has 10,00,000 equity shares throughout the year and profit attributable to equity holders of ₹40,00,000. It has 50,000 10% convertible debentures of ₹100 each, each convertible into 2 shares, outstanding all year. Tax rate is 25%.

mcqs.explain: Basic EPS is ₹40,00,000 divided by 10,00,000 shares, giving ₹4.00. Convertibles are ignored for basic EPS. In practice: present it alongside diluted EPS.
mcqs.topic: Scope and the earnings figure for basic EPS

mcqs.explain: Interest of 10% on ₹50,00,000 is ₹5,00,000; after 25% tax, ₹3,75,000 is added back because it would not be paid on conversion. In practice: use the after-tax amount.
Diluted earnings ₹43,75,000 over 11,00,000 shares (10,00,000 + 1,00,000 on conversion) give ₹3.98, which is below basic EPS, so the debentures are dilutive. In practice: test each instrument.
